note: LB.11a: a Go ROUTE is one node per (method, path), qname `<METHOD> <path>` like every other server parser, so each node is HANDLED_BY only its own handler and an endpoint's HTTP_CALLS reaches only the route of its method. HEAD (ee4a84a, installed wheel): `route:/users` is one node HANDLED_BY listUsers AND createUser and `route:/users/:id` is HANDLED_BY getUser AND deleteUser, so a DELETE call traces into the GET handler. The four edge forbids can only fire once method-shaped nodes exist; HEAD's violation is the path-only node.

forbid.name: route:/users
forbid.note: the path-only node that stacked GET and POST is gone
PRECISION: a GET route is never handled by the POST handler
the quokka-stack defect: a DELETE call never reaches the GET route
